LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.6: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: What is the importance of creating tempo and rhythm in a crawl?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the front crawl technique in swimming,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform the front crawl technique in swimming,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciates own and others' efforts in performing the front crawl technique.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

C. appreciates own and others' efforts in performing the front crawl technique.

2. demonstrate the front crawl skill in swimming, observing (glide, body position, arm action, leg action and breathing) Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability. B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: The learner uses digital devices to watch video clips of front crawl in swimming.

● Learning to learn: The learner learns to demonstrate and practise the front skills with persistence.

Values:
● Love: The learner portrays a caring attitude while working together in executing front crawl skill in swimming.

● Responsibility: The learner observe pool hygiene and safety while swimming,

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety: The learner observes pool safety when practising front crawl during swimming.

Link to other learning areas:

Science and technology: The learner is exposed to concepts of floatation.
